spatial_claims.claim: AD is divided at E into terms AE (greater) and ED, giving collinear arrangement A-E-D
F bisects ED, so EF = FD with E-F-D ordering
G is on AE such that AG times GE = EF squared, giving A-G-E ordering
p and q defined abstractly by p squared = AB times AG and q squared = AB times GE (no spatial placement)

configuration_map: All constructed points lie on a single line segment AD with ordering A-G-E-F-D. Point E divides AD into the two terms of the first binomial. Point F is the midpoint of ED. Point G is on segment AE determined by the rectangle condition AG times GE = EF squared. Lines p and q are abstract magnitudes defined by their squares equaling certain rectangular areas; they are never placed in any spatial configuration. The entire proof operates on commensurability relations between these magnitudes.

All geometric content reduces to collinear point division on a single line segment. There are no 2D spatial configurations, no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no circle arguments, and no triangle constructions. This is a characteristic Book 10 algebraic proposition with no geometric configuration to check.
